student_note: The Creature compares his home to a kennel, a place for animals. He has no human comforts.

speaker: The Creature
quote: Carpeted with straw
sheet_note: The Creature describing the hovel that becomes his home
student_note: The Creature describes the straw covering the floor of his home. He makes the best of his poor shelter.
context: Novel: "carpeted it with clean straw"

speaker: The Creature
quote: Who was I? What was I? Whence did I come?
sheet_note: The Creature questions who and what he is
student_note: The Creature asks who and what he is. He has no family or history to tell him.

speaker: The Creature
quote: Was I a monster, a blot upon the earth?
sheet_note: He believes that he must simply be a monster, because this is how he is treated by others
student_note: The Creature wonders if he is simply a monster, because that is how everyone treats him.
context: Novel: "Was I, then, a monster, a blot upon the earth"

speaker: The Creature
quote: No father had watched my infant days; no mother had blessed me with smiles
sheet_note: The Creature explains that he was deprived of loving parents and a family
student_note: The Creature says he had no loving parents or family. This is why he is so lonely.

speaker: The Creature
quote: I ought to be thy Adam, but I am rather the fallen angel
sheet_note: When he meets him on the mountain, the Creature tells Victor that he should treat him like Adam, but he has become the devil
student_note: The Creature tells Victor he should have been like Adam, God's first loved creation. Instead he feels like a fallen angel, thrown out and cast aside.
technique_notes: Metaphor – “the fallen angel”: The Creature compares himself to Satan cast out of Heaven: once good, now abandoned. | Religious imagery – Adam and the fallen angel: Links to Paradise Lost; Victor, like God, abandoned his creation.
context: Frankenstein lesson 15: the Creature compares himself to Satan.
lesson_techniques: Religious imagery “Adam”; Metaphor “fallen angel”

speaker: The Creature
quote: Broken the only link that held me to the world
sheet_note: The Creature explains that when the De Laceys rejected him, this was a turning point
student_note: The Creature says that being rejected by the De Laceys was a turning point. It broke his last link with humanity.

speaker: The Creature
quote: Forced solitude
sheet_note: The Creature explains how he was completely rejected by the whole of society
student_note: The Creature describes how society completely rejected him. He was left alone.

speaker: The Creature
quote: Shall each man find a wife, and each beast have his mate, and I be alone?
sheet_note: The Creature asks Victor why he should be the only living creature to be alone
student_note: The Creature asks Victor why every man and beast has a partner but he must be alone.
context: Novel: "Shall each man, find a wife for his bosom, and each beast have his mate, and I be alone?"

speaker: The Creature
quote: The love of another will destroy the cause of my crimes
sheet_note: The Creature explains to Victor that if he has a female companion to show him love and kindness, he will no longer be a cruel monster
student_note: The Creature says that if he had a companion to love him, he would stop being cruel.

speaker: The Creature
quote: I, like the arch-fiend, bore a hell within me
sheet_note: The Creature describes how the rage and hatred turns him into a monster and a devil
student_note: The Creature says his rage turned him into a devil. He compares his inner torment to hell, like Satan.
technique_notes: Metaphor – “a hell within me”: His inner torment and guilt are compared to Hell. | Allusion – “arch-fiend”: Refers to Satan in Milton’s Paradise Lost, linking the Creature to the fallen angel.
context: Frankenstein lessons 15-17: links to Satan’s “Myself am Hell”.
lesson_techniques: Metaphor “hell within me”; Allusion to Paradise Lost

speaker: The Creature
quote: My heart swelled with hellish triumph
sheet_note: The Creature feels a sense of power when murdering William
student_note: The Creature feels a sense of power as he murders William. He enjoys it, like a devil.
context: Novel: "my heart swelled with exultation and hellish triumph" | Frankenstein lesson 17.
lesson_techniques: Oxymoron “hellish triumph”

speaker: The Creature
quote: I too can create desolation
sheet_note: The Creature feels a sense of power when murdering William
student_note: The Creature feels powerful when he kills William. 'Too' shows he realises he can cause suffering just as others have caused his.
context: Frankenstein lesson 17: “too” suggests he realises he is like others.
lesson_techniques: Declarative statement

speaker: The Creature
quote: Beware, for I am fearless and therefore powerful
sheet_note: The Creature tells Victor that he is powerful because he has nothing to lose or fear
student_note: The Creature warns Victor that he is powerful because he has nothing left to lose or fear.

speaker: Victor Frankenstein
quote: I was the slave, not the master, of an impulse which I detested yet could not disobey
sheet_note: The Creature tells Walton that he was controlled by his rage and hatred
student_note: Victor says his rage and hatred controlled him. He was a slave to them, not their master.
context: Sheet says The Creature, but in the novel it is Victor speaking (about his urge for revenge), so speaker changed to Victor Frankenstein

speaker: The Creature
quote: Polluted by crimes and torn by the bitterest remorse, where can I find rest but in death?
sheet_note: The Creature tells Walton how he feels internally broken and only death will bring him peace
student_note: The Creature tells Walton he feels broken inside by his crimes. Only death will bring him peace.

speaker: Walton
quote: Undiscovered solitudes
sheet_note: Robert Walton describing the undiscovered and isolated place he travels to
student_note: Walton describes the unexplored, isolated place he travels to.

speaker: Walton
quote: Dear Margaret, do I not deserve to accomplish some great purpose?
sheet_note: Walton suggesting that he is destined for greatness and feels entitled to success
student_note: Walton writes to his sister that he deserves to succeed. He feels destined for greatness and entitled to it.

speaker: Walton
quote: I bitterly feel the want of a friend
sheet_note: Walton describing how lonely and isolated he feels on his voyage
student_note: Walton says he is lonely on his voyage and wants a friend.

speaker: Walton
quote: The brother of my heart
sheet_note: Walton describing his deep friendship and connection with Victor
student_note: Walton describes his deep friendship with Victor. He feels they are as close as brothers.

speaker: Walton
quote: One man’s life or death were but a small price to pay for the knowledge which I sought
sheet_note: Walton describing how he is determined to succeed, but this also shows how reckless he is
student_note: Walton says one man's life or death is a small price to pay to succeed. This shows how determined and reckless he is.
context: Novel: "for the acquirement of the knowledge which I sought" (teacher: "for the knowledge which I sought")

speaker: Victor Frankenstein
quote: Whither does your senseless curiosity lead you?
sheet_note: When Walton asks for details about the creation of the Creature, Victor tells him how foolish he is for wanting to go down the path that he went. Shelley suggests that Walton perhaps has not truly learnt from Victor’s example. However, he does turn his ship back home
student_note: Walton asks about how Victor created the Creature. Victor tells him he is foolish to want to know.

speaker: The Creature
quote: I longed to join them, but I dared not
sheet_note: The Creature describes how he desperately wants to be part of their family, but fears that they will reject him, like the others who have attacked or rejected him
student_note: The Creature watches the De Lacey family. He desperately wants to join them, but is afraid they will reject him.
context: Creature watching the De Lacey family; check wording against the teacher sheet (not found word-for-word)

speaker: The Creature
quote: Who can describe their horror and consternation on beholding me?
sheet_note: The creature describes the shock and disgust the De Laceys feel when they see him
student_note: The Creature describes how horrified and disgusted the De Laceys were when they saw him.

speaker: Elizabeth
quote: Sweet laughing blue eyes
sheet_note: In a letter to Victor, Elizabeth describes William’s bright blue eyes
student_note: In a letter to Victor, Elizabeth describes William's bright blue eyes. They show his innocence.
context: Frankenstein lesson 7: William’s eyes show innocence.
lesson_techniques: Symbol “eyes”

speaker: The Creature
quote: This little creature was unprejudiced
sheet_note: The Creature sees William and believes he will be kind to him because he’s an innocent child
student_note: The Creature sees William and thinks he will be kind, because he is a young child who has not learned to be prejudiced.

speaker: William
quote: You are an ogre
sheet_note: William immediately sees the Creature as a monster and treats him cruelly
student_note: William immediately calls the Creature an ogre. He treats him cruelly, so the Creature's hope is crushed.

speaker: Victor Frankenstein
quote: The saintly sufferer
sheet_note: Victor describing Justine Moritz as a pure and innocent victim
student_note: Victor describes Justine Moritz as a pure, innocent victim.

speaker: The Creature
quote: It stirred the fiend within me – not I, but she, shall suffer
sheet_note: The Creature assumes Justine will be cruel to him, so decides to make her suffer
student_note: The Creature expects Justine to be cruel to him, so he decides to make her suffer.

speaker: Victor Frankenstein
quote: The judges had already condemned my unhappy victim
sheet_note: Victor describes how Justine was assumed guilty and not given a fair trial
student_note: Victor says the judges had already decided Justine was guilty. She was not given a fair trial.

speaker: Victor Frankenstein
quote: The tortures of the accused did not equal mine
sheet_note: Victor describes how he is suffering inside even more than Justine
student_note: Victor says he suffers inside even more than Justine, because he knows the truth and stays silent.

speaker: Justine
quote: I began to think that I was the monster he said I was
sheet_note: Justine describing how, after being told she was a monster by the interrogator and so many people, she began to believe she was
student_note: Justine says that after being called a monster so many times she began to believe it herself.
context: Novel: "I almost began to think that I was the monster that he said I was" (the confessor, not the interrogator, says it)

speaker: Elizabeth
quote: Men appear to me as monsters thirsting for each other’s blood
sheet_note: Elizabeth describes how, after Justine’s trial and execution, she considers society to be the true monster
student_note: After Justine's trial and execution, Elizabeth thinks men are the real monsters. She sees society as cruel.
context: Frankenstein lesson 9: said after Justine’s execution; shows Elizabeth’s realisation that society is cruel.
lesson_techniques: Vampiric imagery

speaker: Victor Frankenstein
quote: The image of Clerval was forever before me, ghastly and murdered
sheet_note: Victor is haunted by the image of seeing Clerval’s dead body
student_note: Victor is haunted by the image of Clerval's dead body.

speaker: Victor Frankenstein
quote: My friend and dearest companion had fallen victim to me and the monster of my creation
sheet_note: Victor believes that he is responsible for the murder of Clerval
student_note: Victor believes he is responsible for Clerval's murder. His friend has fallen victim to the Creature.
context: Novel: "Clerval, my friend and dearest companion, had fallen a victim to me and the monster of my creation"

speaker: Victor’s mother
quote: Pretty present
sheet_note: Victor’s mother describes Elizabeth as a present for Victor
student_note: Victor's mother calls Elizabeth a 'pretty present' for Victor. She is treated like an object, not a person.
context: Frankenstein lesson 4: treats Elizabeth as an object.
lesson_techniques: Metaphor “present”; Adjective “pretty”

speaker: Victor Frankenstein
quote: Promised gift
sheet_note: Victor describes Elizabeth as his gift
student_note: Victor calls Elizabeth his 'promised gift'. He treats her like a possession.

speaker: Victor Frankenstein
quote: Till death she was to be mine only
sheet_note: Victor falls in love with Elizabeth and he decides that they will be together forever
student_note: Victor decides that Elizabeth will be his alone until death.

speaker: The Creature
quote: I shall be with you on your wedding night
sheet_note: The Creature promises to get revenge on Victor on his wedding night
student_note: The Creature promises to take revenge on Victor on his wedding night.
context: Appears more than once in the novel; chapter shown is the first.

speaker: Victor Frankenstein
quote: He seemed to jeer, as with his fiendish finger he pointed towards the corpse of my wife
sheet_note: Victor describes the Creature laughing at the dead body of Elizabeth
student_note: Victor describes the Creature laughing at Elizabeth's dead body.

speaker: Victor Frankenstein
quote: My heart often sickened at the work of my hands
sheet_note: Victor describes making the female companion and is disgusted by his work
student_note: Victor is disgusted while making the female creature. His heart sickens at his own work.

speaker: Victor Frankenstein
quote: A race of devils would be propagated upon the earth
sheet_note: Victor worries that the two monsters will have children that will spread across the world
student_note: Victor fears that two monsters will have children who spread across the world.

speaker: Victor Frankenstein
quote: The wickedness of my promise burst upon me
sheet_note: Victor suddenly changes his mind and believes it is a mistake to make another creature
student_note: Victor suddenly realises how wicked it is to make another creature. He changes his mind.

speaker: Victor Frankenstein
quote: A ghastly grin wrinkled his lips
sheet_note: Victor describes seeing the Creature’s smiling face watching his work through the window
student_note: Victor sees the Creature's smiling face watching his work through the window.

speaker: Victor Frankenstein
quote: Inarticulate sounds
sheet_note: The Creature tries to speak to Victor when he is born, but he just makes noises like a baby (on the midpoint list only)
student_note: When he is born, the Creature cannot speak. He makes noises like a baby.
context: Appears more than once in the novel; chapter shown is the first. | Frankenstein lesson 7: childbirth imagery for the Creature’s birth.
lesson_techniques: Imagery (childbirth)
